key_insight: A guided diffusion model can reconstruct phase-limited bubbly-flow velocity fields, including the difficult bubble phase, from sparse 2D slices while preserving key flow statistics.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical route to recover unmeasured or experimentally inaccessible velocities in multiphase turbulence, improving diagnosis and modeling of bubbly flow experiments.
method: Train a diffusion model on 2D velocity slices extracted from fully resolved 3D DNS of buoyancy-driven bubbly flows.
Condition generation on surrounding liquid-flow information to reconstruct missing phase-limited fields.
Use a simple patching scheme across adjacent slices to extend reconstruction toward 3D bubble interiors.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the generated fields are physically realistic and that the bubble-phase reconstructions accurately reproduce key statistical features, with reasonable 3D reconstruction from adjacent slices.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated on DNS-derived slices in a specific pseudo-turbulent regime, so transfer to real experimental data and more complex multiphase settings may require careful validation.
paper_title: Gappy Reconstruction of Bubbly Flows by Guided Diffusion Models
